newsitem.title: CANADA: World feed barley prices up on Saudi demand - CWB.
newsitem.headline: World feed barley prices up on Saudi demand - CWB.

text.p: World feed barley prices should continue their rise on sustained Saudi Arabian demand, a Canadian Wheat Board market analyst said on Monday.

"The feed barley's up. The main reason is strong demand from Saudi Arabia, they imported about 45 percent of world feed barley in the current year and we're expecting them to be another huge player in the coming year," CWB market analyst Larry Sawatzky said.
The CWB boosted its world price estimate by C$4 a tonne for No1 Canada Western Feed Barley to the C$126.00 to C$156.00 a tonne range in-store Vancouver or St. Lawrence.
That's up 3.3 percent from April's world price estimate for No1 CW feed barley at C$122.00 to C$152.00.
Another supportive factor was inadequate rain fall on drought stressed European barley acreage, Sawatzky said.

"Southern Europe, particularly Spain, got some rain but it was too late to prevent yield loss in that area so that's positive in terms of the price outlook because they may have less barley available to export," Sawatzky said.
Saudi Arabia imported an annual average of 4.81 million tonnes of barley since 1986, CWB statistics show. Saudi Arabia may import 6.0 million tonnes in calendar 1997, analysts said.
"There's no question, Saudi Arabia's the key factor in the world feed barley market. They may account for that much (45 percent of world barley trade) in the coming crop year," Sawatzky said.
